root_cause: Undersized partition count for the peak traffic profile
resolution_steps_taken: Confirm scope: check throughput and consumer lag per topic and partition to isolate the affected pipeline. >> Inspect broker leader distribution and recent restart or deployment events on the affected brokers. >> Stabilize consumption: pause non-critical consumers, then restart the affected consumer group with an increased session timeout. >> Rebalance partition leadership and verify replication lag returns to zero on all replicas. >> Replay or reprocess any messages that exceeded retention during the outage window and confirm end-to-end counts with the source. >> Monitor lag and throughput for 30 minutes against baseline before closing the incident.

root_cause: JVM garbage collection pauses from an undersized heap
resolution_steps_taken: Identify the unhealthy node from the cluster health endpoint and cordon it from client traffic. >> Check disk, heap, and garbage collection logs on the affected node to confirm the resource bottleneck. >> Free space or expand the volume if disk pressure is the driver; restart the node process if memory pressure persists after a heap dump is captured. >> Reassign replicas from the failed or degraded node and watch under-replicated partition counts return to zero. >> Raise the heap or throttle background compaction if GC or CPU saturation is the confirmed driver, then schedule the permanent fix. >> Verify all nodes report green status and client error rates are back to baseline before closing.

root_cause: Field explosion from unbounded dynamic mappings
resolution_steps_taken: Confirm the bottleneck is indexing, not query load: compare indexing latency p95 and queue depth against search latency. >> Inspect segment counts and merge activity; force a merge only during a low-traffic window if segment counts are extreme. >> Reduce bulk request sizes and split oversized batches so segments stay within the target size range. >> Raise the refresh interval to the agreed value for high-volume indices and re-check latency after one full cycle. >> Review dynamic mapping settings and add explicit mappings for new fields to stop field explosion. >> Track indexing latency p95 and queue depth for one hour to confirm the improvement holds under normal load.

root_cause: Schema registry compatibility level raised without a migration
resolution_steps_taken: Diff the current configuration against the last known good version in the change log to isolate the offending change. >> Roll back the single offending setting first rather than the whole change set, and note the rollback in the incident record. >> Restore the service account permissions or compatibility level that the change altered, using the principle of least privilege. >> Restart only the affected component so the corrected setting takes effect with minimal blast radius. >> Validate with a smoke test: produce, consume, and index a synthetic record end to end. >> Add the setting to the pre-deployment checklist and require a second reviewer for that configuration class.

root_cause: Broker leader election loop after a rolling restart
resolution_steps_taken: Confirm scope: check throughput and consumer lag per topic and partition to isolate the affected pipeline. >> Inspect broker leader distribution and recent restart or deployment events on the affected brokers. >> Stabilize consumption: pause non-critical consumers, then restart the affected consumer group with an increased session timeout. >> Rebalance partition leadership and verify replication lag returns to zero on all replicas. >> Replay or reprocess any messages that exceeded retention during the outage window and confirm end-to-end counts with the source. >> Monitor lag and throughput for 30 minutes against baseline before closing the incident.

root_cause: Corrupted batch files delivered by an upstream partner feed
resolution_steps_taken: Identify the failing connector or source from the ingestion error stream and pause it to stop error amplification. >> Compare a sample of rejected records against the registered schema to find the exact mismatch or corruption pattern. >> Restore source connectivity: reset the exhausted connection pool or restart the failed connector task. >> Quarantine malformed records to the dead letter queue with the rejection reason attached for later replay. >> Apply the schema mapping fix or partner feed correction, then resume ingestion at a reduced rate. >> Backfill the gap window from the source and reconcile record counts before closing the incident.
